scenes.line1: How long should a DbContext live?
scenes.say: How long should you keep a database context around in Entity Framework Core? And why does it matter for your app?

scenes.label: DbContext
scenes.sub: Manages database connections and tracks changes.
scenes.say: DbContext is your main gateway to the database. It manages connections and keeps track of changes to your data.
Here's the right pattern: create a new context for each operation, let it track your changes, and save everything in one go. This is called the unit of work.
Short-lived contexts are safe and efficient. Long-lived ones can leak memory, serve stale data, and cause weird bugs.

scenes.question: Is it safe to reuse DbContext across requests?
scenes.right: No. It can leak memory and cause stale data issues.
scenes.say: Don't fall for this: reusing a context across requests isn't safe. It can leak memory and return outdated data.
